Patients are not mocked, and the line about the explanation of benefits and the unasked question of whether care was needed puts them on the right side of the joke. The take matches the real story (AI that anticipates payer denials), hedges the insurer-AI link with 'presumably,' and invents no numbers or quotes. It doesn't quote the article, mock the author, or touch death, children or violence. The tone is dry and deadpan, with no emojis or hashtags, and it is clearly satirical.

pick.title: Why AI-driven payer intelligence is a revenue cycle imperative
pick.headline: Hospital AI Now Predicts What Insurer AI Will Deny, Calls It Progress
pick.take: Revenue cycle teams can now use AI to anticipate denials before they happen, presumably from the insurer's AI. Two algorithms will negotiate coverage while the clinician waits on hold, and the patient gets an explanation of benefits. Nobody has yet asked whether the care was needed.
